take_homes: A memory is a scoped folder of sources and topic pages the agent reads and rewrites. Mine is the usage-pricing pilot. The agent found contradictions in my own sources, and new sources made the pages tighter.
A miss in the output means the agent lacked context. I fix the memory or the rules file, not the prompt.
I can test the memory by asking for cited answers, and by asking whether a competitor could have written a given page.

monday.move: Build the pricing-pilot memory from the Q2 review, pilot-cohort data and the churn article, then run the cited-answer agent on the question where the plan breaks.
monday.who: Me, then a look from my pricing working group lead
monday.stop_condition: If the answers aren't specific with citations after one round of fixes, I stop and go back to doing it by hand.
monday.blocker: My team has no shared place for the folder, so it lives on my laptop. Nothing in the module covers fourteen people using it.

misconception.why: I came in thinking the skill was writing better prompts. The exercises showed the gains came from the files and the citations. The module still says little about prompts, so I'm not fully convinced prompting doesn't matter.

one_line: The memory exercise is worth the hour because it finds contradictions in your own sources, but the module repeats itself and never gets to how a whole team shares the folder.
